claims.text: By default the jobs of a workflow run have no dependencies and run in parallel; jobs.<job_id>.needs makes a job wait until the named jobs complete successfully (and skips it if one fails, unless a condition such as always() is used).
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: Workflow syntax for GitHub Actions > jobs.<job_id>.needs; Using jobs in a workflow

claims.text: Each job runs on its own runner; with GitHub-hosted runners every job gets a fresh machine, so files (and Docker images) a job leaves on its disk are not available to another job.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: About GitHub-hosted runners (a new VM per job); Using jobs in a workflow

claims.text: Run 36332055445 (push to master, 7a131bc = stage-2): the jobs with no needs (test, app, lab, manifests) started at 16:07:24-25Z on four runners; image started after test completed; staging and publish started after image completed.

Artifacts let a job persist files after it completes and share them with another job in the same workflow run; actions/upload-artifact uploads them, actions/download-artifact downloads them by name; they stay attached to the run after it ends.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: Storing and sharing data from a workflow (workflow artifacts); actions/upload-artifact and actions/download-artifact README

claims.text: ci.yml@stage-2 lines 74-83: step 'Save both images to one file' runs docker save --output images.tar donhang-api:stage-2 donhang-migrate:stage-2, then actions/upload-artifact@v4 with name: images, path: images.tar.

ci.yml@stage-2 lines 89-102: staging has the if: push-to-master condition, needs: [test, image], environment: staging, then checkout, actions/download-artifact@v4 with name: images, and docker load --input images.tar.

docker save writes one or more images, with their names (tags), to a tar archive (--output file); docker load reads such an archive and restores the images and their names, printing 'Loaded image: <name>' for each.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: docker image save, docker image load; tested locally (scratchpad ci-d) with the stage-2 images

claims.text: actions/download-artifact with name: and no path: writes the artifact's files into the job's working directory ($GITHUB_WORKSPACE), so images.tar appears where docker load --input images.tar reads it.
claims.source_hint: actions/download-artifact README (path default: $GITHUB_WORKSPACE); run 36332055445 staging log 'Starting download of artifact to: /home/runner/work/don-hang/don-hang'

claims.text: In run 36332055445 the image job logs 'SHA256 digest of uploaded artifact zip is 8b6f4793…'; staging and publish each log 'SHA256 digest of downloaded artifact is 8b6f4793…' (same fingerprint of the stored file) and the two 'Loaded image:' lines.

In run 36332052090 (push to branch auto/stage-2, same commit) staging and publish were skipped by their if:, and the image job still uploaded the artifact images (artifact 10936425184 listed on the run).

Dependency caching is for reusing files that do not change often across jobs or runs; artifacts are for saving files a job produces (built output, logs) and sharing them between jobs of a run or viewing them after the run.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: Dependency caching reference > Comparing artifacts and dependency caching

claims.text: A cache is repository-scoped and looked up by key (restore-keys can match another run's entry); GitHub may evict entries; on a miss actions/cache does not fail the step, so a missing file makes a later step (docker load) fail instead.
claims.source_hint: actions/cache README (outputs cache-hit); GitHub Docs: Dependency caching reference > usage limits and eviction policy

claims.text: actions/download-artifact@v4 with name: fails the step when no artifact with that name exists in the run (for example, before the uploading job has uploaded it), which fails the job.
claims.source_hint: actions/download-artifact README / source (getArtifact throws 'Artifact not found for name'); GitHub Docs: Storing and sharing data from a workflow

claims.text: Workflow artifacts can be downloaded from the workflow run summary page after the run has completed, until they expire.

claims.source_hint: executed in Git Bash on Docker 28 with the stage-2 images (scratchpad ci-d)

claims.text: scripts/up.sh@stage-2 runs docker compose up with --build, which builds the api and migrate images (donhang-api:stage-2, donhang-migrate:stage-2) on the learner's machine.

Without needs:, staging would start with test while image still waits for test; its download-artifact step would ask for images before image uploaded it and fail; a job without needs: is also not skipped when test fails.
